question: Given that $P = \begin{bmatrix}2 & -1 \\ 3 & 4\end{bmatrix}$, $Q = \begin{bmatrix}5 & 2 \\ 7 & 4\end{bmatrix}$ and $R = \begin{bmatrix}2 & 5 \\ 3 & 8\end{bmatrix}$, find a matrix S such that PQ - RS is a null matrix.
explanation:
Step 1 Formulate the required equation. Setting $PQ - RS = O$ is mathematically equivalent to $RS = PQ$. The first step is to calculate the matrix product $PQ$.

Step 2 Perform the multiplication of matrices $P$ and $Q$. We calculate $PQ = \begin{bmatrix}2 & -1 \\ 3 & 4\end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix}5 & 2 \\ 7 & 4\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}(2)(5)+(-1)(7) & (2)(2)+(-1)(4) \\ (3)(5)+(4)(7) & (3)(2)+(4)(4)\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}10-7 & 4-4 \\ 15+28 & 6+16\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}3 & 0 \\ 43 & 22\end{bmatrix}$.

Step 3 Substitute this result into our equation to get $RS = \begin{bmatrix}3 & 0 \\ 43 & 22\end{bmatrix}$. To solve for matrix $S$, we need to multiply both sides of the equation by $R^{-1}$ on the left, giving $S = R^{-1}(PQ)$.

Step 4 Find the inverse of matrix $R$. First, calculate the determinant: $|R| = (2)(8) - (5)(3) = 16 - 15 = 1$. The adjoint of a $2 \times 2$ matrix is found by swapping diagonal elements and negating off-diagonal elements, yielding $\text{adj } R = \begin{bmatrix}8 & -5 \\ -3 & 2\end{bmatrix}$. Therefore, $R^{-1} = \frac{1}{1} \begin{bmatrix}8 & -5 \\ -3 & 2\end{bmatrix}$.

Step 5 Multiply $R^{-1}$ by the previously calculated $PQ$ to find $S$. $S = \begin{bmatrix}8 & -5 \\ -3 & 2\end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix}3 & 0 \\ 43 & 22\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}(8)(3)+(-5)(43) & (8)(0)+(-5)(22) \\ (-3)(3)+(2)(43) & (-3)(0)+(2)(22)\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}24-215 & 0-110 \\ -9+86 & 0+44\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}-191 & -110 \\ 77 & 44\end{bmatrix}$.
